225: Tokyo Tribes by Santa Inoue (Tokyopop) is a gritty street-gang story with a hip-hop beat. In an alternate Tokyo, the city is carved up by rival youth gangs called tribes, each ruling its own neighborhood. Kai, of the laid-back Musashino crew, finds himself pulled into a feud with his former friend Mera, who runs with a far more violent tribe. It's loud, stylish, and full of street fights, a good pick for readers who like delinquent and gang stories.
227: Worst by Hiroshi Takahashi (DMP) is a delinquent action story set in the same world as Crows. Hana Tsukishima, a cheerful country boy with a huge appetite and serious fists, arrives at Suzuran All-Boys High, a school where the toughest fighters rule. He has one simple goal: to become the strongest guy at Suzuran. It's a story about fistfights, loyalty, and friendship, perfect for fans of classic school-brawler manga.
228: The Twelve Kingdoms by Fuyumi Ono (Tokyopop) is a sweeping fantasy novel series about finding your strength. Youko Nakajima is an ordinary, people-pleasing high school girl until a mysterious golden-haired man named Keiki appears in her classroom and sweeps her away to a strange world of twelve kingdoms. Alone and hunted, she has to figure out who she is and why she was brought there. It's a thoughtful, richly built world for readers who love serious fantasy.
229: Big Hero 6 by Haruki Ueno (Yen Press) is a heartfelt superhero adventure based on the Disney film. Hiro Hamada is a fourteen-year-old robotics genius in the city of San Fransokyo, and his big brother Tadashi has built a gentle, inflatable healthcare robot named Baymax. When tragedy strikes, Hiro and Baymax team up to uncover a mystery. It's funny, warm, and action-packed, great for younger readers and fans of the movie.
231: Nekogahara: Stray Cat Samurai by Hiroyuki Takei (Kodansha) is a samurai action story starring cats. In a feudal world ruled by pampered house cats, strays live hard lives on the margins. Nora, a scruffy, sharp-tongued ronin cat with a deadly sword, wanders into trouble everywhere he goes. From the creator of Shaman King, it's full of stylish sword fights and dark humor, ideal for readers who like samurai stories with a twist.
233: Saving 80,000 Gold in Another World for My Retirement by FUNA (Kodansha) is a lighthearted isekai comedy. After losing her family, Mitsuha Yamano discovers she can travel back and forth between modern Japan and a medieval fantasy world. Being practical, she sets a goal: save up 80,000 gold coins so she can retire comfortably. It's a cozy, clever story about a girl using modern know-how to get ahead, great for fans of easygoing fantasy.
237: The Most Heretical Last Boss Queen by Bunko Matsuura (Seven Seas) is a fantasy story about rewriting your own fate. A young girl realizes she has been reborn as Pride, the cruel villain queen of an otome game she once played, destined to make everyone miserable before meeting a terrible end. Determined to change course, she sets out to protect the people she was meant to hurt. It's a warmhearted villainess story for fans of reincarnation fantasy.
238: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu Academy by Koyoharu Gotouge (Viz Media) is a goofy school comedy spin-off of Demon Slayer. Tanjiro, Nezuko, Zenitsu, Inosuke, and the rest of the cast are reimagined as students and teachers at a modern high school, where the Hashira run the classrooms and the dress code is enforced with passion. It's light, silly, and full of in-jokes, a fun treat for fans who want to see the characters in a relaxed setting.
241: My Sassy Girl by Ho Sik Kim (Comics One) is a romantic comedy based on the story that inspired the hit Korean film. Gyeon-woo, an easygoing college student, steps in to help a drunk young woman on a subway train and ends up responsible for her. She turns out to be bossy, unpredictable, and hard to forget, and soon he's swept into her chaotic life. It's sweet and funny, great for readers who enjoy offbeat romance.
242: No Longer Human by Usamaru Furuya (Vertical) is a dark psychological drama adapted from Osamu Dazai's classic novel and set in modern Tokyo. Yozo Oba has always felt unable to understand other people, so he hides behind a mask of clowning and charm. As he drifts into adulthood, that mask starts to crack. It's a haunting, serious read for mature readers interested in literary adaptations and character studies.
243: Beck by Harold Sakuishi (Kodansha) is a coming-of-age story about music and friendship. Yukio "Koyuki" Tanaka is a bored fourteen-year-old with no direction until he rescues a strange patchwork dog and meets its owner, Ryusuke Minami, a talented guitarist trying to start a band. Soon Koyuki picks up a guitar of his own. It's funny, honest, and full of the excitement of rock music, perfect for anyone who's ever dreamed of being in a band.
247: Words Bubble Up Like Soda Pop by Imo Oono (Yen Press) is a gentle summer romance based on the anime film. Cherry is a shy boy who wears headphones to block out the world and only expresses himself through haiku. Smile is a bubbly girl who hides her braces behind a face mask. When they meet by chance at a shopping mall, a quiet friendship begins. It's sweet and colorful, ideal for readers who like soft, feel-good love stories.
249: Didn't I Say to Make My Abilities Average in the Next Life?! Everyday Misadventures by FUNA (Seven Seas) is a comedy spin-off of the isekai fantasy series. Mile was reborn in another world and asked for perfectly average abilities, but ended up wildly overpowered instead. These short, lighthearted chapters follow Mile and her party, the Crimson Vow, through daily life and silly side adventures. It's breezy fun for fans of the main series.
250: The Dawn of the Witch by Kakeru Kobashiri (Vertical) is a fantasy adventure set in the world of Grimoire of Zero. Saybil is a magic student who has lost his memories and is close to flunking out of school. He's sent on a special field course alongside the legendary and mischievous witch Loux Krystas, heading to a land where witches and magic are still feared. It's an inventive, character-driven fantasy for readers who like magic schools and mysteries.
251: Appleseed by Masamune Shirow (Dark Horse) is a classic cyberpunk action story. After a devastating world war, Deunan Knute, a tough young soldier, and her cyborg partner Briareos are brought to Olympus, a gleaming utopian city run by artificial intelligence and genetically engineered humans. They join the city's police force, but paradise has its own dangers. It's packed with detailed tech and political intrigue, ideal for fans of Ghost in the Shell and hard sci-fi.
255: The Horizon by JH (Ize Press) is a quiet, haunting drama about survival. In a world torn apart by war, a young boy who has lost everything meets a girl who is just as alone. Together they set out walking toward the horizon, facing a ruined landscape and the cruelty of the adults they meet along the way. It's a moving, emotional read for older readers who appreciate thoughtful, literary stories.
256: Adachi and Shimamura by Hitoma Iruma (Yen Press) is a gentle slice-of-life yuri romance. Adachi and Shimamura are two high school girls who skip class and end up hanging out in the gym loft, playing ping-pong and talking about nothing in particular. As their friendship grows, Adachi starts to wonder whether she feels something more. It's a soft, slow-burn story for readers who enjoy quiet, emotional romance.
257: Battle Angel Alita: Last Order by Yukito Kishiro (Viz Media) is a cyberpunk action series that continues the classic Battle Angel Alita. Alita, a cyborg warrior with a fierce sense of justice, is brought back to life by the brilliant and dangerous scientist Desty Nova. Waking up in a new body, she sets out to uncover the secrets of the floating city of Zalem. It's intense and inventive, perfect for fans of hard-hitting sci-fi.
258: One Piece by Eiichiro Oda (Viz Media) is a long-running pirate adventure full of heart and humor. The New World saga picks up as Monkey D. Luffy and his Straw Hat crew reunite after two years of training and set sail into the New World, the most dangerous stretch of sea on the Grand Line. It's packed with huge battles, colorful characters, and big emotions, a great continuation for anyone following Luffy's dream of becoming King of the Pirates.
260: Tsubasa: Reservoir Chronicle by CLAMP (Del Rey) is a fantasy adventure that hops between worlds. When Princess Sakura's memories scatter across dimensions as magical feathers, her childhood friend Syaoran makes a deal with the Dimensional Witch to find them. He's joined by the gruff ninja Kurogane and the cheerful magician Fai. It's full of action and cameos from other CLAMP stories, great for readers who love sweeping, romantic fantasy.
262: Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World by Okama (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance set during an endless war. Iska is a young swordsman fighting for the Empire, which wages war against the nation of witches. On the battlefield he meets Aliceliese, a powerful witch princess and his sworn enemy. The two are drawn to each other even as their countries want them to fight. It's an action-filled star-crossed love story for fans of fantasy romance.
263: Black Summoner by Doufu Mayoi (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure about a man who loves a good fight. Reborn in another world, Kelvin gives up his memories in exchange for incredible powers and becomes a summoner who calls monsters to his side. He quickly discovers that what he really craves is battling strong opponents. It's a fun, fast-paced isekai for readers who like overpowered heroes and plenty of action.
265: Crest of the Stars by Hiroyuki Morioka (Tokyopop) is a space opera about two very different worlds. When the Abh, a long-lived, blue-haired spacefaring people, take over his home planet, young Jinto Lynn becomes a member of their nobility in a single day. Sent off to train with the Abh, he meets Lafiel, a proud young officer who is also a princess. It's thoughtful, detailed science fiction for readers who love interstellar politics and adventure.
268: Infinite Dendrogram by Sakon Kaidou (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy adventure set inside a virtual-reality game. Ray Starling logs into Infinite Dendrogram, a brand-new VRMMO said to be as real as the real world. His starting companion turns out to be Nemesis, a sharp-tongued girl who can transform into a weapon. As Ray explores, he discovers the game's people and stakes may be more real than anyone expected. It's great for fans of game-world stories.
269: Kieli by Yukako Kabei (Yen Press) is a gothic fantasy about a lonely girl and a strange traveler. Kieli can see ghosts, which makes her an outsider at her strict church boarding school. One day she meets Harvey, a quiet drifter who turns out to be an undead soldier, along with his talking radio companion. Together they set off on a journey across a dusty, desolate world. It's moody and touching, ideal for readers who like found-family road stories.
270: Kieli by Yukako Kabei (Yen Press) is a gothic fantasy novel about a lonely girl and a strange traveler. Kieli can see ghosts, which makes her an outsider at her strict church boarding school. One day she meets Harvey, a quiet drifter who turns out to be an undead soldier, along with his talking radio companion. Together they set off on a journey across a dusty, desolate world. It's moody and touching, ideal for readers who like found-family road stories.
272: Marginal Operation by Shinobu Fujiwara (J-Novel Club) is a military thriller about an unlikely commander. Arata is a thirty-year-old with no job and no direction, so he takes a position with a private military company overseas. There he's put in charge of a unit of child soldiers and discovers he has a surprising talent for strategy. It's a serious, thought-provoking story for readers who enjoy realistic military drama.
273: Monster Girl Doctor by Yoshino Origuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy with a medical twist. Glenn Litbeit runs a clinic in Lindworm, a city where humans and monsters live side by side, and his patients include centaurs, mermaids, harpies, and more. With his lamia assistant Sapphee, he takes on every strange case that comes through the door. It's playful and inventive, great for readers who like monster-girl stories with a caring lead.
275: My Friend's Little Sister Has It In For Me! by Mikawa Ghost (J-Novel Club) is a romantic comedy about a guy who just wants to be left alone. Akiteru Ooboshi is a no-nonsense high schooler focused on efficiency and his part-time game-making work. Unfortunately, his best friend's little sister, Iroha, loves to tease him and treats his apartment like her own. Only he gets to see her mischievous side. It's fun, flirty, and full of banter.
276: Secrets of the Silent Witch by Matsuri Isora (Yen Press) is a fantasy story about a powerful mage who would rather hide. Monica Everett is one of the kingdom's Seven Sages, a genius who can cast magic without saying a word, but she's painfully shy and avoids people. Then she's ordered to go undercover at a prestigious academy to secretly guard the second prince. It's charming and clever, ideal for readers who love school-set fantasy.
277: Sword Art Online: Fairy Dance by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure set inside virtual reality. Kirito has escaped the deadly game world of Aincrad, but Asuna, the girl he cares about, still hasn't woken up. When he hears a rumor that someone resembling her has been spotted in a fairy-themed online game called ALfheim Online, he logs in to find her. It's a fast-moving adventure for fans of the anime and game-world stories.
278: Sword Art Online by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure novel series set inside virtual reality. In the Fairy Dance arc, Kirito has escaped the deadly game world of Aincrad, but Asuna still hasn't woken up. When he hears that someone resembling her has been spotted in a fairy-themed online game called ALfheim Online, he logs in to find her. It's a fast-moving adventure for fans of the anime and game-world stories.
281: The Most Notorious "Talker" Runs the World's Greatest Clan by Mahiro Maki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story about winning with brains instead of brawn. Noel Stollen dreams of becoming the greatest hunter like his grandfather, but his class, the Talker, is considered the weakest there is. Refusing to give up, he decides to use strategy, scheming, and sheer nerve to build the strongest clan in the land. It's sharp and satisfying for fans of underdog heroes.
284: Wolf & Parchment: New Theory Spice & Wolf by Isuna Hasekura (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure set in the world of Spice and Wolf. Col, once a young traveling companion of Holo and Lawrence, has grown up and sets off on a journey to reform a corrupt Church. Tagging along is Myuri, Holo and Lawrence's spirited daughter, who has wolf ears and a tail of her own. It's thoughtful and warm, a natural next read for Spice and Wolf fans.
285: Woof Woof Story by Inumajin (Yen Press) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. An overworked man dreams of a lazy life, so when he's reborn in another world as a puppy, he plans to be a pampered pet. There's just one problem: he's actually a Fenrir, a legendary wolf of tremendous power. As he grows, keeping his easy life gets more and more complicated. It's cute and silly, great for fans of laid-back isekai.
287: The Mythical Detective Loki Ragnarok by Sakura Kinoshita (ADV) is a supernatural mystery with a mischievous hero. Loki, the Norse trickster god, has been banished to Earth in the body of a young boy. To get home, he runs a detective agency that hunts down evil spirits. His cheerful assistant Mayura is obsessed with the supernatural but has no idea who he really is. It's fun, spooky, and lighthearted, great for fans of mythology.
288: Please Teacher! (Onegai Teacher) by Shizuru Hayashiya (Comics One) is a sci-fi romantic comedy. High schooler Kei Kusanagi is stunned to find out that his new homeroom teacher, Mizuho, is actually an alien on a secret mission to Earth. When he accidentally discovers her secret, the two end up married to cover it up, and they have to hide it from everyone at school. It's goofy and sweet, ideal for fans of early-2000s anime comedies.
291: FLCL by Hajime Ueda (Tokyopop) is a wild, surreal coming-of-age story based on the cult-classic anime. Naota is a twelve-year-old who thinks nothing interesting ever happens in his sleepy town. Then a strange woman on a Vespa named Haruko runs him over and whacks him on the head with a bass guitar, and robots start emerging from his forehead. It's chaotic, stylish, and funny, perfect for readers who like the offbeat and unpredictable.
292: Blank Slate by Aya Kanno (Viz Media) is a dark action story about a man with no past. Zen is a ruthless criminal in a war-torn land who doesn't remember who he is or where he came from. Those who cross his path have reason to fear him, and those who try to learn his secrets risk even more. From the creator of Otomen, it's moody and stylish, a good pick for readers who like antiheroes.
302: Beast Master by Kyousuke Motomi (Viz Media) is a sweet and funny shojo romance. Yuiko loves animals, but they all run away from her because she's a bit too enthusiastic. Then she meets Leo, a new transfer student with a wild side and an unusual connection to animals, who scares most of their classmates. Yuiko decides he's the perfect friend. From the creator of Dengeki Daisy, it's a charming read for fans of quirky romance.
305: Magic Knight Rayearth II by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure that continues the story of Magic Knight Rayearth. Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu, three Tokyo schoolgirls who once fought as Magic Knights in the world of Cephiro, find themselves called back. Cephiro is in turmoil, and the girls must face new enemies and difficult questions about their first journey. It's a heartfelt follow-up for fans of classic magical girl fantasy.
316: Maoh: Juvenile Remix by Kotaro Isaka (Viz Media) is a suspense thriller about power and persuasion. Ando is a high schooler who hates going along with the crowd. In a city on edge, a charismatic young politician named Inukai is rising fast, and Ando suspects something sinister behind his popularity. At the same time, Ando discovers he has a strange power to make others say what he's thinking. It's tense and thought-provoking, great for fans of psychological thrillers.
323: Mobile Suit Gundam Wing by Koichi Tokita (Mixx) is a sci-fi action story about rebellion and giant robots. In the future, space colonies live under the control of the Earth Sphere Alliance. To strike back, five young pilots are sent to Earth, each with a powerful Gundam mobile suit. One of them, the cold and mysterious Heero Yuy, begins his mission. It's packed with mech battles, a fun read for longtime fans of the anime.
326: Yowamushi Pedal by Wataru Watanabe (Yen Press) is an energetic sports story about bicycle racing. Sakamichi Onoda is a shy anime fan who rides his old granny bike to Akihabara and back every week, a long and hilly trip. When his classmates notice how strong a rider he is, they recruit him into the school's cycling club. It's full of heart, friendship, and nail-biting races, perfect for anyone who loves an underdog sports story.
327: Rurouni Kenshin: Restoration by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a samurai action story that retells the beginning of Rurouni Kenshin. In early Meiji-era Japan, a gentle wanderer named Kenshin Himura carries a reverse-blade sword and has vowed never to kill again, despite his past as a feared assassin. When he meets Kaoru, who runs a struggling dojo, he finds a place to belong. It's a quick, fresh take on a classic.
328: Wolf's Rain by Toshitsugu Iida (Viz Media), based on the anime by studio Bones, is a moody post-apocalyptic adventure. Wolves were believed to be extinct, but some survive by disguising themselves as humans. Kiba, a lone white wolf, follows the scent of a mysterious flower that he believes will lead to a hidden Paradise. Along the way, he crosses paths with other wolves with their own reasons to search. It's atmospheric and bittersweet, ideal for fans of the anime.
332: Nisemonogatari: Fake Tale by NISIOISIN (Vertical) is a talky, supernatural mystery novel in the Monogatari series. Koyomi Araragi, a high schooler with a vampire past, finds his younger sisters Karen and Tsukihi, who fancy themselves defenders of justice, mixed up with a con man spreading fake curses. Koyomi has to step in, even if it means taking on his sisters too. It's witty and full of clever dialogue, perfect for fans of the anime.
333: Rent-A-(Really Shy!)-Girlfriend by Reiji Miyajima (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy spin-off of Rent-A-Girlfriend. Sumi Sakurasawa is cute and kind, but she's so shy she can barely speak to strangers. Determined to change, she takes a job as a rental girlfriend, where she goes on dates with paying customers. With help from her coworkers, she tries to become a great date one shy step at a time. It's sweet and lighthearted fun.
334: Pretear by Kaori Naruse (ADV) is a fantasy romance with a fairy-tale spin. Himeno Awayuki is a spunky girl who has just moved into a wealthy new stepfamily that doesn't welcome her. Then she meets seven handsome Leafe Knights who reveal she's a Pretear, a girl who can merge with them to fight a dark force draining life from the world. It's a magical girl story with a Snow White twist, ideal for fans of classic shojo.
341: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords by Akira Himekawa (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure based on the Nintendo game. When the evil sorcerer Vaati escapes and kidnaps Princess Zelda, Link draws the legendary Four Sword and is split into four copies of himself, each with his own personality. The four Links have to learn to work together to save Hyrule. It's bright, funny, and adventurous, perfect for younger readers and Zelda fans of any age.
351: The God of High School by Yongje Park (Webtoon) is a high-energy martial arts action manhwa. Jin Mori is a carefree high schooler with incredible fighting skills, and he enters a nationwide tournament that pits the best young fighters in Korea against each other. The winner is promised any wish they want. As the fights grow more intense, it's clear the tournament is hiding something bigger. It's fast and explosive, great for fans of battle stories.
352: Strawberry Panic by Sakurako Kimino (Seven Seas) is a romantic yuri drama set at elite girls' schools. Nagisa Aoi transfers to St. Miator, one of three prestigious Catholic girls' academies sharing a hilltop campus. On her first day she meets Shizuma, the school's dazzling and admired top student, and is instantly swept off her feet. It's a dreamy, dramatic school romance for readers who enjoy classic girls' love stories.
358: Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online by Keiichi Sigsawa (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action spin-off of Sword Art Online. Karen Kohiruimaki is a very tall college student who is self-conscious about her height. In the gun-filled VR game Gun Gale Online, she finally gets to be tiny as her pink-clad avatar, LLENN, and discovers she's a surprisingly deadly player. It's fast and fun, great for fans who want more action-focused SAO.
361: Murder Princess by Sekihiko Inui (Broccoli Books) is a fantasy action comedy about a body swap. When her kingdom is attacked, Princess Alita flees and collides with Falis, a ruthless bounty hunter, and the two accidentally switch bodies. Now the gentle princess is stuck as a wanderer, while the fierce fighter has to play the role of royalty and protect the throne. It's quick, funny, and full of sword fights, great for fans of fantasy action.
368: The Wallflower by Tomoko Hayakawa (Del Rey) is a goofy romantic comedy. Sunako Nakahara loves horror movies, skeletons, and dark rooms, and wants nothing to do with people. When her aunt leaves her mansion in the care of four gorgeous high school boys, they're promised free rent if they can turn Sunako into a proper lady. It's a cheerfully chaotic makeover story, ideal for readers who love slapstick humor and gothic flair.
369: Backstage Prince by Kanoko Sakurakouji (Viz Media) is a sweet shojo romance set in the world of kabuki theater. Akari is an ordinary high school girl who takes a part-time job at a kabuki theater. There she meets Ryusei, a rising young star who is cold and distant to the people around him but has a soft spot for animals. As Akari gets closer to him, she starts to see his real self. It's a cute pick for romance fans.
370: Abenobashi Magical Shopping Arcade by Satoru Akahori (Tokyopop) is a zany comedy adventure based on the anime. Sasshi and his childhood friend Arumi live in Osaka's old Abenobashi shopping arcade, which is about to be torn down. When a strange accident strikes, the two are hurled into one bizarre parallel world after another, from fantasy quests to sci-fi battles. It's fast and silly, great for readers who love genre parodies and wacky humor.
387: RahXephon by Takeaki Momose (Viz Media) is a sci-fi mecha story based on the anime. Ayato Kamina is a quiet teenager living in Tokyo, which he believes is the last city left after a mysterious war. When strange invaders attack, a girl named Haruka finds him and he ends up piloting a giant, mysterious robot called RahXephon. Soon he learns his world isn't what he thought. It's moody and mysterious, ideal for fans of thoughtful mecha stories.
398: My Happy Marriage by Akumi Agitogi (Square Enix) is a romantic historical fantasy. Miyo Saimori grew up mistreated by her stepmother and half-sister in a family where she was the only one born without supernatural gifts. She's sent off to marry Kiyoka Kudo, a commander rumored to be so cold that every past fiancée fled. But Kiyoka is not what she expected. It's a gentle, slow-burn love story for fans of Cinderella-style romance.
405: The Garden of Words by Makoto Shinkai (Vertical) is a quiet romantic drama based on the anime film. Takao is a fifteen-year-old who dreams of becoming a shoemaker and skips class on rainy mornings to sketch in a Tokyo garden. There he keeps running into Yukari, a mysterious older woman who also seems to be avoiding something. A gentle connection grows between them. It's beautiful and melancholy, ideal for fans of Your Name.
406: Servant x Service by Karino Takatsu (Yen Press) is a workplace comedy set in a city government office. Lucy, a young woman with a ridiculously long name, joins the health and welfare department as a new civil servant, along with her fellow rookies Yutaka and Saya. Lucy has a secret reason for taking the job. From the creator of Working!!, it's a light, funny story about everyday office life and quirky coworkers.
407: Corpse Party: Blood Covered by Makoto Kedouin (Yen Press) is a horror story based on the cult-classic video game. A group of high school friends perform a friendship charm before their school is torn down, hoping to stay together forever. Instead, they're torn away to Heavenly Host Elementary, a decaying school haunted by vengeful spirits, and they have to find a way out. It's gruesome and creepy, for older readers who love survival horror.
409: Suki: A Like Story by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a sweet romance with a mystery at its heart. Hinata is a cheerful, childlike sixteen-year-old who lives alone with her many teddy bears. When a handsome new teacher named Asou moves in next door, she quickly falls for him. But Asou has secrets of his own, and somebody may be watching Hinata. It's soft and charming with a hint of suspense, a nice pick for CLAMP fans.
420: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Astray by Toda Yasunari (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mecha adventure set in the Gundam SEED universe. Lowe Guele is a cheerful engineer working for a junk guild that salvages wrecked ships. While exploring a secret colony, his crew stumbles upon a prototype Gundam, and Lowe takes it as his own, landing him in the middle of a war. It's upbeat and full of robot action, great for Gundam fans.
421: Aho-Girl by Hiroyuki (Kodansha) is a gag comedy about the world's most clueless girl. Yoshiko Hanabatake loves bananas, has terrible grades, and has absolutely no common sense. Her long-suffering childhood friend Akkun is the only one who tries to keep her in line, usually with a well-timed smack. Each short chapter is packed with fast, silly jokes. It's perfect for readers who love absurd, laugh-out-loud humor.
422: A Little Snow Fairy Sugar by Haruka Aoi (ADV) is a sweet, gentle fantasy based on the anime. Saga is a busy, serious girl who runs on a strict schedule in a small European town. One day she discovers Sugar, a tiny apprentice season fairy searching for a magical twinkle, whom only Saga can see. Soon Sugar and her fairy friends turn Saga's life upside down. It's cozy and heartwarming, ideal for younger readers.
427: Thus Spoke Rohan Kishibe by Hirohiko Araki (Viz Media) is a collection of eerie supernatural short stories spun off from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure. Rohan Kishibe is a famous and eccentric manga artist who will go anywhere to find inspiration for his work. His curiosity leads him into strange encounters with curses, cursed places, and uncanny people. It's stylish and creepy, great for JoJo fans and readers who enjoy weird tales.
435: Magic Knight Rayearth 2 by CLAMP (Dark Horse) is a fantasy adventure that continues Magic Knight Rayearth. Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu are three Tokyo schoolgirls who once fought as Magic Knights in the world of Cephiro, and now they're called back. Cephiro has fallen into chaos, and the girls must face new enemies and hard questions about their first journey. It's a heartfelt follow-up for fans of classic magical girl fantasy.
436: El Hazard by Ryoe Tsukimura (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure based on the anime. Makoto Mizuhara is a high schooler who discovers a strange woman sealed away in the ruins under his school. In a flash, he's transported to El Hazard, a magical world on the edge of war, where he finds himself caught up in a struggle against an insectlike army. It's lighthearted and fun, ideal for fans of 1990s anime adventures.
437: Lupin III by Monkey Punch (Tokyopop) is a classic caper comedy. Arsène Lupin III is the grandson of the famous gentleman thief, and he lives up to the name as a master burglar and charming rogue. Along with gunman Jigen, swordsman Goemon, and the alluring Fujiko, he pulls off outrageous heists while dodging the dogged Inspector Zenigata. It's slick and stylish, a fun pick for fans of heist stories and vintage manga.
438: Sorcerous Stabber Orphen by Yoshinobu Akita (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure about a wandering sorcerer. Orphen is a gifted young sorcerer who left the prestigious Tower of Fangs to search for Azalie, the woman he thinks of as a sister, after a magical accident transformed her into a dragon. With a pair of troublemaking sidekicks, he travels the land looking for a way to save her. It's a fun classic for fans of 1990s fantasy.
445: Nekogahara: Stray Cat Samurai by Hiroyuki Takei (Kodansha) is a samurai action story starring cats. In a feudal world ruled by pampered house cats, strays live hard lives on the margins. Nora, a scruffy, sharp-tongued ronin cat with a deadly sword, wanders into trouble everywhere he goes. From the creator of Shaman King, it's full of stylish sword fights and dark humor, ideal for readers who like samurai stories with a twist.
